Watts made this hymn from Psalm 78, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth. 2I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning, 3that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us. 4We will not hide them from their children, but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might, and the wonders He has performed. … 68 more verses PSALM 78 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 78
When some were slain, the rest return'd, And sought the Lord with tears; Under the rod they fear'd and mourn'd, But soon forgot their fears. STANZA VII
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 3. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
